The CSSF Eastern Route Programme delivers against the objectives in the UK’s National Security Council Illegal Migration Strategy.The Programme includes projects designed to support and continue to build capacity in Turkey’s frontline migration institutions and develop Turkey’s migration policy framework, working with the Directorate General of Migration Management (DGMM), the Ministry of Interior, the Ministry of Labour and others.  In Greece the Programme supports the EU-Turkey deal by providing specialist deployments to the EU Commission in Athens, expert support to the European Asylum Support Office, and interpreters to the Greek island ‘hotspots’. In Serbia the Programme contributes to capacity development of asylum and migration authorities’ adherence to international standards in the area of asylum and migration, including by using UK expertise.

The CSSF Eastern Route Programme delivers against the objectives in the UK’s National Security Council Migration Strategy. In Greece the Programme supports the EU-Turkey deal by providing specialist deployments to the EU Commission in Athens, expert support to the European Asylum Support Office, and Greek island ‘hotspots’.

The CSSF Eastern Route Programme seeks to ensure that the migration management mechanisms in Turkey, Greece and the Balkans develop in a way which promotes social cohesion and addresses the migration challenges presented by large migrant populations; that migrants are expediently and efficiently processed utilising proper safeguards; and that refugees’ rights, including rights to asylum are upheld.  Projects are designed to support and continue to build capacity in Turkey’s frontline migration institutions and develop Turkey’s migration policy framework in a manner consistent with international norms and standards.  Turkey currently lacks the capacity to effectively process newcomers, particularly from Syria.  Working with the Directorate General of Migration Management (DGMM), the Ministry of Interior, the Ministry of Labour, Social Services and Family and others, projects seek to improve capacity in: protection and services referral to the most vulnerable elements of the migrant population including, women, children and the disabled; and, which addresses social cohesion challenges from hosting c4m migrants. Flexibility of the programmes enables us seek out and fill gaps in the larger FRIT programme that DFID supports.  In Greece the Programme supports the EU-Turkey deal by providing specialist deployments to the EU Commission in Athens and providing expert support to the European Asylum Support Office. These deployments aid with expediting caseworking processes to get quicker decisions and more effective implementation of the deal, easing capacity pressures and humanitarian conditions on hotspot islands. The Programme also supports the deployment of interpreters to the Greek Reception and Identification Service, who support migrants on arrival at hotspot islands; ensuring orderly entry to the Greek asylum system as well as helping the most vulnerable get the support they need. In Serbia the Programme contributes to capacity development of asylum and migration authorities’ adherence to international standards in the area of asylum and migration, including by using UK expertise.

titles: Reintegration and Support for Returnees (RSR) Programme
descriptions: The CSSF Reintegration and Support for Returnees Programme aims to increase the capacity of countries through provision of sustainable reintegration to returning migrants to reintegrate back into their home country and re-engage with their local community.

The CSSF Reintegration and Support for Returnees Programme delivers against the objectives in the UK Government’s Illegal Migration Strategy.  The Programme aims to increase the capacity of countries to manage the return of migrants through provision of post-arrival and reintegration support and by prison institution building. Activity in the Programme comprises of immediate post-arrival support; basic reintegration support through vocational or educational training and signposting to services; and capacity building through the provision of infrastructure and equipment, and training and expertise.

The CSSF Returns and Reintegration Programme delivers against the objectives in the UK’s National Security Council Illegal Migration Strategy. The Programme aims to increase the capacity of countries to manage the return of migrants  through provision of post-arrival and reintegration support and by institution building (including prison reform). Activity in the Programme comprises immediate post-arrival support; reintegration support through vocational or educational training and signposting to services available; capacity building through the provision of infrastructure and equipment; and training and expertise. This programme is comprised of ODA funding targeted to support a safe supported return home for illegal migrants.   It’s primary purpose is to ensure those migrants are properly supported in a human rights-compliant manner on return to their home countries, alleviating known pressures on host communities and generating micro-economic benefits.  We are therefore directly supporting poverty reduction objectives.

The CSSF Upstream Programme delivers strategic communication interventions targeting key audiences in prioritised countries. The interventions aim to provide targeted information on safe migration to address the welfare concerns of those that have, or are planning, to migrate irregularly to ensure they are better informed of the risk, opportunities and realities of migration.

The CSSF Upstream Strand delivers strategic communication interventions targeting key audiences in prioritised countries in Africa and South Asia regions. The interventions aim to provide targeted information to those that have, or are planning, to migrate irregularly to ensure they are better informed of the risk, opportunities and realities of migration. It also uses targeted capacity-building of border and asylum management systems and law enforcement in source and transit countries to restrict and reduce illegal migration pathways, disrupt organised immigration crime and improve protection arrangements for vulnerable groups at risk of exploitation.

titles: Addressing key drivers and enablers of irregular migration from northern Albania
descriptions: The programme seeks to address drivers and enablers of irregular migration from the North of Albania in order to enable people to have a better future in their own communities and country. The programme seeks to achieve this by increasing resilience and reducing vulnerability to push and pull factors. Key project components will consist of locally-targeted employment and private sector development activities, anchored in a strong social component transforming the way individuals and communities relate to irregular migration. This will be supported by a targeted messaging campaign and active engagement of youth who are most at risk for irregular migration. This meets the DAC directives on migration, primarily beneficial to the host community in Northern Albania with its focus on sustainable development outcomes over the lifetime of the programme. Only ODA eligible spend reported on.

titles: Improving Referrals and Services for Migrant and Refugee Survivors of Gender-Based Violence and Human Trafficking in Serbia
descriptions: The programme assists migrant and refugee survivors of human trafficking, exploitation and other forms of GBV, on a key and growing migrant transit route. The programme offers tools and resources (through workshops, meetings, and training) to the most vulnerable to improve their situation and become more resilient. It also engages with the Serbian government leading to improvement in the identification and referral systems which significantly impact the treatment of vulnerable migrants. The programme has also worked to re-establish an informal co-ordination and exchange of information between state and non-state actors. This programme meets the DAC specific directives on migration
